02 / Define the target first

One tomato is different from one cluster.

Individual fruit

One box per visible tomato

Original AgRob fruit boxes and ripeness labels were combined into one tomato class. Corrected fruit labels were not included in this run.

SplitImagesFruit boxes

20 buffer images were excluded. Development images were viewed during the earlier baseline.

Visual clusters

One box per labeled group

The completed export contains images and cluster boxes. Groups are nearby tomatoes that appear to share a stem. Botanical truss membership is unverified. The export’s split assignments were preserved.

SplitImagesCluster boxes

zero-cluster images: 15 train, 3 validation, 1 test. One 0.01-pixel edge overshoot was clipped and recorded. Cluster boxes map to one model class.

Shared method: standard fruit DETR initializer → replace head with one target class → train 15 epochs on RTX 3070 → choose confidence on validation → score the fixed checkpoint. Resize within 480 × 480; dynamic padding; best checkpoint selected by validation loss. This is standard DETR, separate from RT-DETR.

Say this

  • Fruit labels describe individual tomatoes; cluster labels describe groups.
  • We trained separate models because those boxes mean different things.
  • Validation picks the confidence threshold. Evaluation measures error after settings are fixed.

03 / Establish the starting point

The original Tomato class detected nothing.

The unadapted fruit checkpoint was evaluated at confidence 0.30 on the same 152-image sequence later used for development.

Tomato-class detections
Supplied fruit labels
Count error · fruit/image

What this told us

The pretrained checkpoint needed greenhouse-specific adaptation. It missed every labeled fruit with the Tomato class.

An all-fruit diagnostic counted other classes such as Apple, but aligned with almost none of the tomato boxes. It was not accepted as a tomato-counting result.

Conclusion: the unadapted checkpoint did not meet the counting requirement.

Say this

  • We first tested the model as supplied, before adapting it to our images.
  • It produced no Tomato-class detections, so the error was 12.118 fruit per image.
  • This gave us a measured starting point and a reason to fine-tune.

07 / Agree on the next experiment

Improve the labels, then test model changes.

  1. Agree on the counting rule

    Define singleton groups, hidden fruit, image-edge groups, and unclear stems. Confirm whether the target is visual clusters or verified trusses.

  2. Review and version the labels

    Resolve missing fruit and inconsistent group boundaries with a second annotator. Keep the original export and publish corrected labels as a new version.

  3. Separate scenes across splits

    Keep nearby frames and the same plants together. Reserve a fresh final set, including confirmed empty scenes. Viewed test images become development material.

  4. Run controlled comparisons

    Repeat the 480-pixel baseline first. Then try 640-pixel input and other changes one at a time on the same validation set.

  5. Freeze settings and test once

    Choose checkpoint and confidence on validation. Evaluate the fresh final set with count error, precision/recall, and reviewed failures.

  6. Share a reproducible handoff

    Record dataset version, model hash, split, threshold, results, and examples. Agree on an acceptable error target before declaring the baseline complete.

Decision for the team: confirm the completed cluster labeling rules, review the new failure examples, and choose a fresh scene-separated final set. No agreed accuracy acceptance target is recorded yet.
